P53 shipped Windows on gcc's inline `xchgl`/`movl` pair, reasoning that no Windows image exported the generic entries. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 that the second half of that reasoning was never true, only inferred from the narrower fact that MICROSOFT ships none: mingw-w64's `libatomic-1.dll` — beside the gcc that IS this platform's C reference — exports `__atomic_load` (ord 55) and `__atomic_store` (ord 71), while ucrtbase, vcruntime140, kernel32, msvcrt and ntdll export ZERO between them and MSVC's own bundled compiler-rt defines none. All four pe64 flavours now declare the role, so the `windows` arm below takes the SAME libcall route as every other leg. ⚠ WHAT THE WINDOWS RUN VERDICT PROVES IS UNCHANGED AND STILL NARROW: x86-64 tolerates the misaligned access, so rc 42 here proves NO FAULT and that the value round-tripped — it does NOT prove ATOMICITY, and the pre-fix binary returned 42 too. The property that matters is the ROUTE, and the route is pinned where every host can see it (`tests/lir/test_mir_to_lir`'s `ShippedPe64FormatRoutesTheUnderAlignedAccessToTheRuntime`, which asserts BOTH the libcall for `g.a` AND the surviving native `xchg` for `h.a`). ✔MEASURED on this host, debug AND release: the emitted image imports `__atomic_store`/`__atomic_load` from `libatomic-1.dll`, keeps exactly one native `xchg` for the aligned control, and RUNS rc 42. ⓘ THE WINDOWS ARM NOW HAS A LOAD-TIME DEPENDENCY THIS EXAMPLE DID NOT HAVE BEFORE: `libatomic-1.dll` is NOT in-box on Windows (✔MEASURED: absent from System32, resolved from `C:\Strawberry\c\bin` on PATH). That is the mingw-w64 runtime shipped with the gcc this repo already requires to BUILD on Windows, so the gate leg's prerequisites are unchanged in practice — but a Windows host with no mingw on PATH would red THIS ARM ONLY, and the failure would be a loader error naming the DLL rather than a wrong answer. ✔MEASURED that the dependency is PAY-PER-USE and does not leak into ordinary binaries: a program with no `_Atomic` at all, and a program whose every `_Atomic` access is naturally ALIGNED, both import `ucrtbase.dll` ALONE. ★★★ P54 LANE `la` — THE ROUTE IS UNCHANGED AND THE PROVIDER IS NOT, AND EVERY MEASUREMENT ABOVE STILL STANDS. The under-aligned member still lowers to `__atomic_load`/`__atomic_store`; what changed is WHO defines them on Windows. `libatomic-1.dll` is not in-box on Windows, and depending on it was ruled a workaround — so the pe64 `atomicsRuntime` role now names a `source`, `runtime/platform/src/atomic.c`, which DSS compiles for this very target and the linker pulls out of the shipped runtime archive by name. ✔MEASURED on this host: the emitted image imports **ucrtbase.dll ALONE** (the load-time dependency this arm gained in the previous cycle is GONE), the four locked primitives (`xchg %edx`, `xchg %rdx`, `lock cmpxchg` at 32 and 64 bits) are IN the image, the naturally-aligned control still keeps its native `xchg`, and it RUNS rc 42. ⚠ THE WARNING ABOVE ABOUT WHAT rc 42 PROVES IS STILL EXACTLY RIGHT and is why this example gained a SIBLING: x86-64 tolerates the misaligned access, so rc 42 proves NO FAULT and a round trip, never ATOMICITY. The atomicity property now has its own execution witness in `examples/c/packed_atomic_member_concurrency`, where threads race an object deliberately placed to straddle a cache line — and ✔MEASURED there, three runs out of three, the pre-fix native form is caught TEARING (rc 11) while the shipped route returns 42.
$comment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER (P53): runtime witness for an UNDER-ALIGNED `_Atomic` scalar access — an `_Atomic int` at byte offset 1 of a `__attribute__((packed))` struct — beside a naturally-aligned CONTROL of the same type in a non-packed struct. exit = 7 + 35 = 42. ⚠⚠ READ THE RUN VERDICT HONESTLY: three of the four arms below CANNOT SEE THIS DEFECT and never could. qemu-user does not enforce the LDAR/STLR alignment check, and x86-64 tolerates a misaligned access outright, so the PRE-FIX binary also exits 42 under `qemu-aarch64`, on pe64/Windows and on elf64-x86_64 — ✔MEASURED both directions at this tree. The arm that CAN see it is `darwin` (native Apple Silicon, `emulator: ""`, which enforces the same check Apple clang compiles for), and the decisive measurement was taken OFF the corpus entirely, on a native aarch64 Linux host: the same source, one artifact md5-verified on both ends, `rc 135 Bus error (core dumped)` with the target key mutated back to `remainsAtomic` and `rc 42` as shipped. ★ WHAT THIS EXAMPLE THEREFORE ADDS ON THE BLIND LEGS IS THE CONTROL, NOT THE FAULT: `h.a` must keep the target's NATIVE inline atomic instruction while `g.a` takes the libcall, so a 'fix' that routed every `_Atomic` access through the runtime — which would pass any fault-only test — reds the emitted-form pins in `tests/lir/test_mir_to_lir` instead of shipping. The `release` arm additionally proves the minted extern call survives Mem2Reg/CSE/LICM/DCE (a dropped atomics call would read an uninitialized slot and change the exit). ANTI-FOLD: `g` and `h` are mutable globals, so neither access is constant-foldable.
